prize_parts.citation: for empirical analyses of how technology and import competition reshape labour demand, local labour markets and wage inequality

statement.case_for: My preferred part is unchanged from round 1: B022 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. What changed is how narrowly I now want it worded and which alternatives I carry. I judge B022 on three criteria: originality, how well the findings have been tested, and whether the credit can be attributed exactly. On originality, the China-shock papers turned a broad question into a measurable one. They showed that exposure to import competition produces local labour-market adjustment that is slow and costly, and they did so with transparent designs. On testing, the evidence has been replicated, re-analysed and contested for about a decade. That contest concerns the size and duration of the effects, not whether adjustment costs exist, so the contested parts are visible and the core finding has survived. On attribution, Autor, Dorn and Hanson are joint authors of the central papers, and Autor is the common thread to the technology strand. The citation should therefore rest on the empirical evidence about technology and import shocks and should not claim the task-model theory, whose originators (Acemoglu, Levy, Murnane) are outside the credited set. My answer to the chair's wording question is that I would support exactly the wording above and would not add 'conceptual'. On B012 versus B022, I do not think they are separable on subject matter, since one is trade theory and the other is the distributional consequences of shocks. On common criteria, B012 has a very strong and long-confirmed core. Its credit boundary, however, is exposed to the parallel Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum work, while the boundary of the B022 citation can be set by wording. I treat that as a close judgement, not a decisive one. I would not oppose B012 if the Committee prefers it, and for that reason it is now my first alternative.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the quantitative claims remain contested. These include the size and persistence of the China-shock effects, the sensitivity of shift-share designs and the long-run interpretation of local adjustment. Even a carefully worded citation leaves a gap, because the task framework that frames the technology half of the story has originators outside the credited set. A narrow empirical citation may therefore understate technology and leave the prize looking mainly like a trade-shock award. The 2024 prize on technology and institutions is thematically adjacent, although I regard its core result as distinct. B022 is also a design and measurement contribution, not a conceptual model such as B012 or B007, and some members will weigh that against it. Finally, B012 has the longer and more direct confirmation record on microdata. If the Committee gives that heavy weight, B012 may be the better choice.

responses.point: Hassler moved from B021 to B012 on attribution grounds. He argues that firm heterogeneity has broader and better-confirmed reach than Grossman-Helpman (B007), that the two ballots compete for Helpman, and that the lobbying model's empirical record is mixed. In round 1 he also proposed only Autor and Hanson for B022 because the credit is blurred.
responses.response: I accept his argument about B007. The mixed empirical record of the lobbying model and the overlap on Helpman are the reasons I no longer lead with it. I have moved B007 to a second alternative, behind B012. On B022, I take his attribution worry as an argument for tighter wording, not for dropping Dorn, who is a full co-author of the core China-shock papers. His own move from B021 was driven by attribution, and the same test applied to B022 gives a clean answer only if the citation is about the empirical shock evidence. I agree the Scientific Background should address the persistence re-analyses directly.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B012 first with Helpman and Melitz. He keeps B022 as an alternative that he would not oppose, because he sees B012 as more mature and less revised, and he says B022 may be preferable if societal significance outweighs conceptual foundation. He also cautions that Helpman should be honoured through B012 or B007 but not both.
responses.response: His argument on maturity is fair, and I have taken it seriously. The firm-heterogeneity core has had more time and has been revised less. My reply is that B022's evidence base is also about two decades old and has been exposed to harsher critique, and the debate over its magnitudes has not overturned the central finding. I agree with his point on Helpman and would not combine B012 and B007 in one award. I also agree that the choice between B012 and B022 turns on how the Committee weighs conceptual foundation against evidence on how people and places are affected. That is a weighting judgement, not a scientific deficiency in either. I am not claiming B022 is better on confirmation alone.

responses.point: Teorell prefers B022 with the trio. He argues that B012 and B022 cover different ground, that the 2024 prize concerned institutions and not the redistributive effects of technology and trade shocks, and that B047 may sit too close to the 2024 prize.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and with his reading that the 2024 overlap with B022 is thematic. His argument about B047 has moved me. If proximity to 2024 counts against B022, it counts more heavily against a prize on constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity. I have therefore dropped B047 from my alternatives, which I had ranked second in the opening. I differ slightly on the non-competition point. The Committee can award only one part, so the two ballots do compete in practice, even if they address different subjects. That is why I state the criteria I use to compare them.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B022 first with the trio and words the citation as 'empirical and conceptual analyses'. She argues the finding that adjustment is slow and costly has survived re-analyses and that Katz's strongest claims lie elsewhere.
responses.response: I agree on the trio, on Katz, and on the point that the debate concerns magnitude and persistence, not direction. I would remove 'conceptual' from the citation. The credited set cannot support a claim on the task framework, because its originators are partly outside the ballot. The empirical wording is what the credited authors can fully carry. I would not want the prize to claim more than the attribution supports, and I think this wording answers the chair's question without losing the technology channel.

responses.point: Boppart prefers B012 with Melitz and Helpman, names B022 as his first alternative, and says he would keep B007 only as an alternative for Helpman. He argues that the firm-heterogeneity framework has the wider footprint in microdata, productivity and growth.
responses.response: His case on breadth is strong and I do not dispute it. I have moved B012 into my alternatives because of it. I disagree only on how decisive the footprint is. A wide footprint measures influence within economics, and I weigh the originality and the exactness of the credit alongside it. On credit, his own uncertainties list Bernard-Jensen, Eaton-Kortum and Redding as unresolved. I regard that as a real cost, comparable to the task-framework issue for B022, and I do not think it clearly favours B012. I agree that B007 should not be paired with B012.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee can agree on a citation anchored in the China-shock and local-labour-market evidence that does not claim the task-model theory whose originators lie outside the credited set.

How far the continuing re-analyses of China-shock magnitude and persistence, and the critiques of shift-share designs, should qualify the award. I take them to concern size and duration, but I cannot settle that from the supplied evidence.

Whether B012 or B022 should come first on common criteria. I regard this as a close weighting of conceptual foundation and breadth of confirmation against evidence on distributional adjustment, not a clear difference in merit.
Whether the 2024 prize's thematic proximity is a timing judgement or a view on merit. I treat it as a timing consideration only.
Whether Dorn is the right third name if the Committee narrows the award, and whether a two-person Autor-Hanson award would be more defensible than I judge.
My attribution judgements rest on my own reading and recollection of the literature and the supplied round-1 files. I have not independently verified them.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1 and none apparent from the supplied profile. My listed co-authors and collaborators (in matching, kidney exchange, refugee resettlement, school choice and auctions) do not appear among the credited names on B022, B012 or B007. I note that Kerstin Enflo is a Lund colleague and that I share SSE affiliations with some committee colleagues. Neither connects to any credited candidate. I have also not co-authored with the credited names on the alternatives I now name, and I do not adjudicate any of these connections.
